notes: ROBOTS: www2.hm.com/robots.txt groups ClaudeBot / Claude-Web / anthropic-ai with GPTBot and PerplexityBot and that whole UA group ends 'Allow: /' (only PetalBot is disallowed) - read on this same host by the IT sibling SR 123; H&M explicitly PERMITS Claude, so no section-5 stop condition. Not re-fetched here because it is the identical host and identical file (efficiency rule 7c). ACCESS: Claude-in-Chrome connector only, in my own tab. www2.hm.com/fr_fr pages loaded normally and same-origin fetch() from that page context returned fully server-rendered HTML with __NEXT_DATA__ intact on all ~85 requests this session (paced 0.25-0.9s apart) - zero 403 / 429 / Akamai challenge at any point, matching the IT sibling rather than the UK sibling (SR 89) which was Akamai-blocked on every HTML route. No curl, WebFetch, proxy or reader service was used. SITE URL: the French locale uses the localised department slug 'maison' (not 'home'); https://www2.hm.com/fr_fr/maison.html is the live Home department, as recorded in the prior Home-Decor pass. TREE - three independent sources taken as a union, per the mandatory sitemap cross-check: (a) the header mega-menu JSON props.pageProps.headerData, which lists 14 product departments under 'Catalogue par produit', of which 'Mobilier' (/fr_fr/maison/catalogue-par-produit/mobilier.html, 875 products) is the only furniture department, and which exposes only 4 mid-level children of it; (b) the full fr_fr category sitemap (fr_fr.sitemap.xml -> 29 x fr_fr.pages.subdepartment.N.xml, 2754 URLs, 328 of them under /fr_fr/maison), which gave the fourth level the mega-menu hides; (c) each PLP's own pill strip plpProps.pills.navigationLinks. The mobilier branch in the sitemap is exactly 20 URLs: department + 3 mid-level nodes + 16 leaves. THE SITEMAP FOUND ONE NODE THE NAV HIDES: furnitures/chairs/pouffes (poufs.html, 35 products) is in neither the mega-menu nor the pill strip. Storage (3 children) and Tables (6 children) agreed exactly between pills and sitemap. NAMING / NODE IDENTITY: every PLP carries plpProps.pills.navigationLinks whose 'path' + 'trackingLabel' is the site's own canonical ENGLISH slug (furnitures/chairs/dining-chairs, furnitures/tables/side, furnitures/storage/wardrobes ...) aliased via 'aliasPath' to the French URL. Each sub_category below is that canonical English node identity, never the French display label - which matters here because the French labels genuinely collide and mislead: the nav pill labelled 'Poufs' points at furnitures/chairs/bean-bags (French h1 'Chaises Sac'), while the real furnitures/chairs/pouffes node is the hidden poufs.html; and the label 'Chaises' is used both for the Chairs parent and for furnitures/chairs/dining-chairs. COUNTS: rendered PLP header 'N produits' (Rule 1, source of truth), read out of the server-rendered HTML for all 16 leaves; it equalled productListingData.totalHits on all 16, and I additionally confirmed the visible rendered header in the live tab on two nodes (Canapes '56 produits', Etageres '44 produits'). Every leaf was fetched twice in this session with identical totals - no drift. REDIRECT / BOGUS-SLUG CHECK (trap 2): run on every leaf - all 16 returned HTTP 200 with final URL == requested URL and canonical == requested URL. The trap is real on this platform and was demonstrated with a control: /fr_fr/home/shop-by-product/furnitures/chairs/zzz-not-real.html returns 200 but silently lands on the Chairs parent (h1 'Chaises', 306) - and /fr_fr/home/shop-by-product/furnitures/chairs/armchairs.html does exactly the same, which is how I established that H&M FR has NO Armchairs node (unlike UK and IT), even though armchair products exist (tagged home_furnitures_chairs_armchairs). By contrast .../chairs/pouffes.html resolved to its own canonical poufs.html with h1 'Poufs' and 35 - a real node. EXCLUDED, with reasons: 'Coussins de siege' (furnitures/seat-cushions), a nav child of Mobilier - seat cushions are textiles and the site also files them under Textiles d'interieur; 'Tout afficher' (view-all) - navigation, per section 3; the whole 'Catalogue par univers' (shop-by-room) tree - it is a parallel ROOM view of the same catalogue, proven by inspecting exterieur/mobilier.html ('Mobilier de jardin', 106 products), whose breadcrumb is home/shop-by-room/outdoor/furniture and whose products carry shop-by-PRODUCT category tags such as home_furnitures_tables_side, i.e. outdoor furniture is already counted inside the Tables / Chairs leaves recorded here (salon/mobilier.html = 609 and chambre-enfant/mobilier-luminaires.html = 41 are the same kind of cross-cut); 'Mobilier et Luminaires' under the Enfants & Bebes product department (55 products) - a MIXED furniture-plus-lighting node whose products are likewise already tagged home_furnitures_* and therefore already inside the Mobilier leaves; the 'Rangement' product department (/rangements.html: Paniers de Rangement, Boites de Rangement, Rangements Muraux) - standalone storage goods and wall storage, out of scope per section 1 and belonging to the future Storage task. SANITY: counts vary correctly by node (1 to 151, never constant), no round display caps; the Mobilier department reports 875 and the three mid-level nodes 306 / 399 / 110 - children do not sum to their parents (295 / 363 / 104) and no parent total was ever copied down to a child. INDEPENDENCE FROM SR 89 (UK) AND SR 123 (IT): distinct locale and URL taxonomy (fr_fr/maison/catalogue-par-produit/mobilier vs en_gb/home/shop-by-product/furniture vs it_it/home/acquista-per-prodotto/arredamento), and materially different assortments on the same nodes - Sofas FR 56 / UK 9 / IT 29, Dining Chairs FR 89 / UK 15 / IT 28, Side Tables FR 151 / UK 61 / IT 76, Cabinets FR 57 / UK 22 / IT 28. FR also has no Armchairs node (UK and IT both do) and, uniquely, exposes both a Bean Bags and a hidden Pouffes node.
